Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead said about it: The finding that a Multiple Tuned Mass Damper system demonstrates stronger robustness when dealing with random pedestrian loads is stated in the A Review on Comfort of Pedestrian Bridges Under Human-Induced Vibrations and Tuned Mass Damper Control Technologies - PMC (E48), and the rule that girders shall be made accessible from the ground, from walkways within the girder bays, or by a Below Bridge Access Vehicle, defined as Below Bridge Access Vehicle (BBAV), is stated in the Bridge Design Manual Section 2 (E49).
Structural Dynamicist said about it: I confirm from dynamics what Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead takes from the A Review on Comfort of Pedestrian Bridges Under Human-Induced Vibrations and Tuned Mass Damper Control Technologies - PMC (E48), that spaced Multiple Tuned Mass Damper, defined as Multiple Tuned Mass Damper (MTMD), tunes ride out drift, which is why twin 400 kg units detuned apart about 1.83 Hz are more robust than one exact unit, and I add for verify-comfort-acceptance the concert-hall decay analogy (C31) where Reverberation Time 60 dB, defined as Reverberation Time 60 dB (RT60), maps to log-decrement damping: pluck the bridge locked then unlocked and pass on measured effective damping, not only on calculation.
Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor said about it: I confirm from comfort what Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead takes from the A Review on Comfort of Pedestrian Bridges Under Human-Induced Vibrations and Tuned Mass Damper Control Technologies - PMC (E48), Structural Dynamicist and Bridge Retrofit Engineer.
Bridge Retrofit Engineer said about it: Static sag 74.7 mm from the static-sag calculation (E63) plus 49.4 mm stroke from the free-decay simulation (E17) totals 124 mm from the envelope calculation (E68), a hand length well below a door width, inside girder depth per the layout sketch (E55), with stop hit 8.40 kN from the stop-force calculation (E66) inside 13.1 kN beam demand; I confirm what Structural Dynamicist takes from the MTMD robustness finding (E48) that detuned twins hold the band, proven by 0.67 m/s2 retrofitted from the crowd build-up simulation (E45) at 0.068 g inside Medium versus 8.28 m/s2 bare from the bare-acceleration calculation (E43) at 0.844 g almost body weight.

statements.text: The finding that a Multiple Tuned Mass Damper system demonstrates stronger robustness when dealing with random pedestrian loads is stated in the A Review on Comfort of Pedestrian Bridges Under Human-Induced Vibrations and Tuned Mass Damper Control Technologies - PMC (E48), and the rule that girders shall be made accessible from the ground, from walkways within the girder bays, or by a Below Bridge Access Vehicle, defined as Below Bridge Access Vehicle (BBAV), is stated in the Bridge Design Manual Section 2 (E49).

I confirm from dynamics what Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead takes from the A Review on Comfort of Pedestrian Bridges Under Human-Induced Vibrations and Tuned Mass Damper Control Technologies - PMC (E48), that spaced Multiple Tuned Mass Damper, defined as Multiple Tuned Mass Damper (MTMD), tunes ride out drift, which is why twin 400 kg units detuned apart about 1.83 Hz are more robust than one exact unit, and I add for verify-comfort-acceptance the concert-hall decay analogy (C31) where Reverberation Time 60 dB, defined as Reverberation Time 60 dB (RT60), maps to log-decrement damping: pluck the bridge locked then unlocked and pass on measured effective damping, not only on calculation.

I confirm from comfort what Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead takes from the A Review on Comfort of Pedestrian Bridges Under Human-Induced Vibrations and Tuned Mass Damper Control Technologies - PMC (E48), Structural Dynamicist and Bridge Retrofit Engineer.

Static sag 74.7 mm from the static-sag calculation (E63) plus 49.4 mm stroke from the free-decay simulation (E17) totals 124 mm from the envelope calculation (E68), a hand length well below a door width, inside girder depth per the layout sketch (E55), with stop hit 8.40 kN from the stop-force calculation (E66) inside 13.1 kN beam demand; I confirm what Structural Dynamicist takes from the MTMD robustness finding (E48) that detuned twins hold the band, proven by 0.67 m/s2 retrofitted from the crowd build-up simulation (E45) at 0.068 g inside Medium versus 8.28 m/s2 bare from the bare-acceleration calculation (E43) at 0.844 g almost body weight.
